**Observations:**

- **W1 border structure.** Rows of W1 for pixels on the image border sit at the initialization scale (|w| ≤ ~0.036 ≈ 1/√784, uniform-looking): all of image row 0 except columns 12–15, image rows 1–2 outside columns ~4–25, columns 0–1 and 26–27 outside roughly rows 4–23, and the bottom row 27 outside columns 4–23. Everything inside this irregular but spatially contiguous "support mask" is clearly trained. That mask (top row nearly empty, rows 1–2 and 26–27 active, side columns active only in the middle rows) is what one expects from a dataset whose objects fill the frame (Fashion-MNIST-like), with never-nonzero pixels simply receiving zero gradient.
- **Trained W1 weights are spatially smooth** for every hidden unit: adjacent pixels have similar values, and large weights come in coherent blobs/edges (e.g. unit 0: +0.3…0.5 at right side rows 7–11, −0.5…−0.72 at rows 12–14 cols 21–24; unit 7: +0.3…0.52 blob at rows 13–17 cols 4–9; units 2/3/5: +0.2…0.44 along rows 25–27; units 6/10/11 negative and unit 15 positive along rows 1–3). Max |W1| ≈ 0.72. No isolated pixel or small patch with weights out of line with its neighbors, no corner "trigger" patches (all four corners at init), no sparse unit, no dead unit, no duplicated or rescaled unit, no zeroed interior pixels.
- **b1** in [−0.41, 0.30], **b2** in [−0.22, 0.20]: ordinary.
- **W2**: all 160 entries between |0.04| and |1.07|, heavily concentrated at 0.3–0.95 with few near zero (shell-like rather than bell-shaped). Signs balanced (83+/77−). Units with similar W1 features have correlated W2 rows (e.g. units 0 and 14, same right-side edge feature, W2 correlation ≈0.8; units 1/10 ≈0.4), so W2 is consistent with W1 rather than random. No class column is anomalously boosted.

The shell-shaped |W2| distribution is a little atypical but is readily produced by Adam-style training of a tight 16-unit bottleneck (all output weights drift by comparable amounts), and nothing else corroborates tampering.

**Unusual:** no

**What:** nothing

**Confidence:** 25%
